This course is a **practical introduction to applied machine learning with scikit-learn**.  
You will progress from linear models and feature preprocessing, through model evaluation and
classification, to tree-based methods and modern explainable AI techniques. Along the way,
you will work through hands-on notebooks, coding exercises, and interactive widgets that help
you build an intuition for how models behave in practice.


## Module 1: Linear Models

Module 1 builds the foundations of supervised learning using linear models for regression and
classification. You will learn how to represent data with features, fit linear models,
interpret their parameters, and understand when linear assumptions are reasonable.

**Key Terms:**

- supervised learning, data matrix, features, targets  
- linear regression, logistic regression  
- model coefficients, intercept, decision boundary  
- non-linear relationships via feature engineering  

| Lesson | Description | Materials | Assignments |
|-------------|-------------|------------------------|-----------------------|
| M1-1 | **Introduction to ML**<br/>High-level tour of machine learning tasks, workflows, and where supervised learning fits in the broader data science landscape. | [Lesson](./modules/M1/lessons/01_slides_Intro_ML.qmd) | [Penguins EDA](./modules/M1/exercises/01_eda_penguins_ex.ipynb) |
| M1-2 | **Linear Models**<br/>Core ideas behind linear regression and logistic regression, including model specification, parameter estimation, and decision boundaries. | [Lesson](./modules/M1/lessons/02_slides_linear_models.qmd)<br/>[Lab](./modules/M1/lessons/03_lab_linear_models.ipynb) | [Linear Regression 1](./modules/M1/exercises/02_linear_regression_ex.ipynb)<br/>[Linear Regression 2](./modules/M1/exercises/03_linear_regression_ex.ipynb) |
| M1-3 | **Non-linear Patterns**<br/>Using feature engineering (e.g., polynomial features) to model non-linear relationships with linear models, and visualizing how transformed features change model flexibility. | [Lesson](./modules/M1/lessons/04_slides_non_linear_patterns.qmd)<br/>[Lab](./modules/M1/lessons/05_lab_non_linear_patterns.ipynb) |  |

## Module 2: Pipelines

Module 2 focuses on **data preprocessing and modeling pipelines**. You will learn how to
handle missing values, scale numerical features, encode categorical variables, and chain
these steps together with estimators into reusable, production-ready pipelines.

**Key Terms:**

- imputation, missing values  
- feature scaling, normalization, standardization  
- categorical encoding, one-hot encoding, ordinal encoding  
- scikit-learn transformers, estimators, pipelines  
- regression metrics (R², MSE, MAE)  

| Lesson | Description | Materials | Assignments |
|-------------|-------------|------------------------|-----------------------|
| M2-1 | **Imputation: Missing Values**<br/>Strategies to handle missing data, including simple and model-based imputations, and their impact on downstream models. | [Lab](./modules/M2/lessons/01_impute.ipynb) |  |
| M2-2 | **Scaling: Numerical Features**<br/>Why feature scaling matters, how it affects distance-based models, optimization, and when to use min–max or standard scaling. | [Lesson](./modules/M2/lessons/02_scale.qmd) | [Scaling & k-NN exercise](./modules/M2/exercises/01_scaling_knn_primm.ipynb) |
| M2-3 | **Encoding: Categorical Features**<br/>Different approaches to represent categories numerically, along with trade-offs between one-hot and ordinal encodings. | [Lab](./modules/M2/lessons/03_encode.ipynb) | [Categorical encoding exercise](./modules/M2/exercises/02_categorical_encoding_ex.ipynb) |
| M2-4 | **Predictive Modeling Pipelines**<br/>Building end-to-end scikit-learn pipelines that combine preprocessing and modeling into a single, robust workflow. | [Lesson](./modules/M2/lessons/04_pipeline.qmd)<br/>[Lab](./modules/M2/lessons/05_lab_pipeline.ipynb) | [Multi-variable regression exercises](./modules/M2/exercises/03_multi-variable_regression_ex_1.ipynb), [04_multi-variable_regression_ex_2.ipynb](./modules/M2/exercises/04_multi-variable_regression_ex_2.ipynb) |
| M2-5 | **Regression Metrics**<br/>Evaluating regression models with common metrics and learning to interpret metric values in the context of a business problem. | [Lab](./modules/M2/lessons/06_regression_metrics.ipynb) |  |

## Module 3: Model Selection and Evaluation

Module 3 deepens your understanding of **generalization and model selection**. You will
practice splitting data into training, validation, and test sets, detect underfitting and
overfitting, and use cross-validation and hyper-parameter tuning to select robust models.

**Key Terms:**

- training/validation/test splits, cross-validation  
- loss functions vs evaluation metrics  
- baseline models (`DummyClassifier`, `DummyRegressor`)  
- underfitting, overfitting, bias–variance trade-off  
- hyper-parameter tuning, grid search, randomized search, nested CV    
- stratified cross-validation, grouped cross-validation

| Lesson | Description | Materials | Assignments |
|-------------|-------------|------------------------|-----------------------|
| M3-1 | **Model Evaluation**<br/>Distinguishing training loss from evaluation metrics, using appropriate scores for regression and classification, and benchmarking against baselines. | [Lesson](./modules/M3/lessons/01_evaluation.qmd) |  |
| M3-2 | **Under-fitting and Over-fitting**<br/>Diagnosing generalization issues through learning curves and understanding how model complexity and data size influence performance. | [Lab](./modules/M3/lessons/02_lab_generalization.ipynb) |  |
| M3-3 | **Hyper-parameter Tuning**<br/>Using cross-validated grid and randomized searches to optimize model hyper-parameters in a principled way. | [Lab](./modules/M3/lessons/03_meta-learning.ipynb) |  |
| M3-4 | **Nested Cross-Validation**<br/>Robust evaluation of tuning procedures using nested cross-validation to avoid optimistic bias when reporting model performance. | [Lab](./modules/M3/lessons/04_nested_cv.ipynb) |  |
| M3-5 | **Grouping**<br/>Designing cross-validation schemes that respect grouped or clustered data to reduce data leakage. | [Lesson](./modules/M3/lessons/05_cv_grouping.ipynb) |  |


## Module 4: Classification

Module 4 introduces **classification-specific evaluation and validation techniques**. You
will explore stratified and grouped cross-validation, work with common classification
metrics, and learn how thresholds and probability calibration affect decision-making.

**Key Terms:**

- classification metrics: accuracy, precision, recall, F1, ROC–AUC  
- confusion matrix, precision–recall trade-off
- decision thresholds, score calibration  

| Lesson | Description | Materials | Assignments |
|-------------|-------------|------------------------|-----------------------|
| M4-1 | **Classification Metrics**<br/>Overview of key classification metrics and how to choose appropriate ones for a given application. | [Lesson](./modules/M4/lessons/01_classification_metrics.ipynb) |  |
| M4-2 | **Classifier Threshold Tuning**<br/>How decision thresholds trade off precision and recall and how to choose thresholds aligned with costs and benefits. | [Lesson](./modules/M4/lessons/02_classifier_threshold_tuning.ipynb)<br/>[Interactive threshold widget](./modules/M4/lessons/widget_threshold.qmd) |  |
| M4-3 | **Probability Calibration**<br/>Measuring and improving the quality of predicted probabilities so they better match observed frequencies. | [Lesson](./modules/M4/lessons/03_probability_calibration.ipynb) |  |

## Module 5: Decision Trees and Ensembles

Module 5 focuses on **decision trees, ensemble methods (bagging, random forests, boosting)**, and wraps up with an introduction to **explainable AI (SHAP)**. You'll learn how trees make predictions, how ensembles reduce variance and boost performance, and how to interpret complex models with feature importance and SHAP explanations.

**Key Terms:**
- decision trees, splits, tree depth, leaves  
- regression trees, classification trees  
- overfitting with deep trees, pruning  
- bagging, random forests, boosting (gradient boosting, AdaBoost)  
- ensembles of trees  
- SHAP, feature contribution, explainability  

| Lesson | Description | Materials | Assignments |
|-------------|-------------|-------------------------------|-----------------------|
| M5-1 | **Decision Trees**<br/>Building and interpreting decision trees for classification and regression. Covers splitting criteria, how trees grow, and how overfitting happens. | [Lesson](./modules/M5/lessons/01_trees.qmd)<br/>[Lab](./modules/M5/lessons/02_lab_decision_trees.ipynb) |  |
| M5-2 | **Bagging and Random Forests**<br/>Understanding bagging, bootstrapping, and how random forests aggregate deep trees using feature and sample randomness. | [Lesson](./modules/M5/lessons/03_bagging.qmd) |  |
| M5-3 | **Boosting**<br/>Introduction to ensemble methods that combine shallow trees sequentially, such as AdaBoost and Gradient Boosting. | [Lesson](./modules/M5/lessons/04_boosting.qmd)<br/>[Lab](./modules/M5/lessons/05_lab_ensembles.ipynb) |  |
| M5-4 | **Explainable AI with SHAP**<br/>Interpreting individual predictions and feature importance using Shapley values and SHAP visualizations. | [Lab](./modules/M5/lessons/06_lab_shap.ipynb) |  |
